fields.features_heading: What Every Open House Answer Records
fields.features_subheading: Describe your listings and who tours them. Emergent turns that into a form and a report the sellers get.
fields.feature_1:
A price opinion from every agent

Ask each visiting agent whether the list price is low, about right, or high, and what they would list the home at. Each answer is saved against the listing and the agent's name.
fields.feature_2:
One link per listing

Give every listing its own form link for the flyer and the broker open invite. Answers file under that address. A weekend with three open houses still reads as three reports.
fields.feature_3:
Agents and buyers, asked different things

The form asks visiting agents about price, condition, and likely buyers. Public visitors get questions about the home and are asked whether they already work with an agent.
fields.feature_4:
Visitors without an agent, ready to call

Visitors who arrive without an agent go to the listing agent's follow-up list with the name and phone number they gave at the door, plus the rating they left on the way out.
fields.feature_5:
A summary the sellers can read

The app writes a short report for the sellers from the feedback and emails it on the schedule you set. Counts come first, then the comments that repeat, word for word as written.
fields.feature_6:
Code your brokerage can keep

On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository when the form needs to sit next to a brokerage's own listing tools. Host it where you like and keep changing it.

fields.usecase_heading: Feedback From the Tour to the Seller
fields.tab_content_1:
Of 12 agents on the tour, 7 call $689,000 high

Brindle Key Realty runs a broker open before a listing goes public. On Tuesday, 12 agents toured 418 Peverell Lane, listed at $689,000, and answered by phone. Seven called the price high, and the lowest suggested list price was $659,000. At 1 PM, listing agent Giada Selvaggio got an email with every answer.
fields.tab_content_2:
For 11 visitors with no agent, a call on Monday

Thistlewick Homes sets a tablet by the door at each open house. On Saturday, 31 visitors signed in at 92 Hackleby Ridge with a name, a phone number, and whether they work with an agent, then rated the home on the way out. The 11 without an agent went to Yannick Okafor-Price's follow-up list for a call on Monday.
fields.tab_content_3:
From 24 visitors, one Monday email for the sellers

Vesna Duarte promised sellers Piotr and Dagny Wyszynski a report after every open house weekend. The app emails it at 8 AM on Monday. This weekend, 24 visitors came to two open houses at 15 Orrin Court, and 18 left a comment. Nine praised the kitchen, and six mentioned road noise in the back bedroom.
fields.tab_content_4:
Which listings 6 or more agents call too high

Marguerite Solis manages 18 active listings at Tollwain Realty Group, all in one table. A listing goes on her price review list when 6 or more agents call the price high. Three are there this week, led by 27 Dunwiddie Street at 9 of 14. She reviews each one with its listing agent before the next open house.

fields.howto_title: How to Collect Open House Feedback
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to create an agent open house feedback form that gets price opinions to you and your sellers, then build it with Emergent.
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Keep visitor questions on the home
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Give each listing its own link
fields.howto_step_1_des: Write down who walks through your open houses: agents on a broker open tour, public visitors, or both. Agents can judge price and condition. Visitors can tell you how the home felt to live in for an hour. One form can ask each group its own questions.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Have touring agents rate the price on a three-step choice, then ask for the list price they would set. A number gives the sellers something concrete to weigh. Add one open comment box after it for anything the choices miss, such as a dated bathroom.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Ask visitors what they liked and what gave them pause, and keep every question about the house itself. The Fair Housing Act prohibits discrimination because of race, color, national origin, religion, sex, familial status, and disability. A visitor form has no reason to touch any of them.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Create one link per listing and print it on the flyer by the door and in the broker open invite. Every answer then belongs to that address, and the report for one home never mixes in comments left at another.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Decide which answers reach the sellers and which stay with you. Send counts and the comments that came up more than once, and keep one-off remarks for your own notes. Pick the day and hour the report goes out, such as Monday morning.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Mark visitors who have no agent so they land on a follow-up list with their phone number, and decide who calls them and by when. At a brokerage, also set the number of agents calling a price high that sends a listing to the managing broker.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Build it and test one weekend
fields.howto_step_7_des: Describe the form and the seller report to Emergent in plain English, and it builds both. Answers go to a database you own. Run the form at one open house, read the first report, and change any question by prompting.

faq_plan.q: What is an agent open house feedback form?
faq_plan.a: An agent open house feedback form is what a listing agent uses to collect opinions on a home from the people who tour it. At a broker open, that means other agents judging the price and condition. At a public open house, it means visitors saying what they thought and whether they have an agent.

faq_plan.q: How do I create an agent open house feedback form?
faq_plan.a: Describe the open house and who tours it to Emergent's AI form builder, for example a broker open where agents rate the price and suggest their own. Emergent builds the form and the database behind it from that prompt. You change any question or report later by prompting again.

faq_plan.q: What should an agent open house feedback form ask other agents?
faq_plan.a: Ask for a judgment on price and the number they would list at, then for condition and the buyer the home suits best. Close with one open comment box. Put the price question first, because it is the answer the sellers ask about before any other.

faq_plan.q: Should an agent open house feedback form ask agents and visitors the same questions?
faq_plan.a: No. Use one link per listing, but let the first question split the two groups. Agents get questions on price and how the home compares with nearby listings. Visitors get questions about how the home felt. Leave price to the agents, whose read on the local market is what the sellers want to hear.

faq_plan.q: How many questions should an agent open house feedback form have?
faq_plan.a: Keep it to five or six. Visitors answer on a tablet or phone near the front door, and every extra question costs answers. Put the one you need most first, such as the overall rating. A visitor who stops early still leaves you something to report.

faq_plan.q: Can visitors fill out an agent open house feedback form without giving a name?
faq_plan.a: Yes, if you make the name optional on the feedback questions and keep it on the sign-in. Some visitors write more freely when no name is attached. Visitors who skip their name cannot go on a follow-up list. Mark which answers can be traced back and which cannot.

faq_plan.q: How do I sort comments from an agent open house feedback form?
faq_plan.a: Read it by listing, not by date. Count how many people raised the same point, then decide with the sellers whether it calls for a fix, a price change, or nothing. A general feedback form can collect the comments that arrive later by email into the same table.

faq_plan.q: Can an agent open house feedback form alert me when an agent submits it?
faq_plan.a: Yes. The app Emergent builds can send an email, a Slack message, or an in-app alert for each answer, or hold them for one summary when the tour ends. A summary suits a busy broker open, while single alerts suit a slow Sunday with a handful of visitors.

faq_plan.q: Does an agent open house feedback form work on a phone?
faq_plan.a: Yes. It opens from a link on any phone or tablet, and Emergent can build it as a conversational flow with one question per screen. That layout suits an agent answering between two showings, since each tap moves to the next question without scrolling past the rest.

faq_plan.q: Who owns the answers collected by an agent open house feedback form?
faq_plan.a: You do. Every answer is saved to a database you own, and forms carry no response caps, which matters in a busy spring of open houses. On paid plans, Emergent can export the codebase to GitHub if your brokerage wants to run the form on its own servers.

faq_heading: Agent Open House Feedback Form FAQ

plan.angle: Searchers for this term want a feedback form a listing agent hands out at an open house, and the pages that answer it are printable sheets with a list of questions. None shows where the answers go next. This page shows a working form for four moments: agents giving a price opinion at a broker open, public visitors signing in at the door, the weekly report the sellers read, and a managing broker seeing which listings draw price complaints. Every answer is saved to a database the brokerage owns.
